paragraphs: Here is what I love about Hezekiah, friend. He gets a threatening letter, and he doesn't hide it, argue with it or stew over it. He takes it up to the house of the LORD and spreads it out before the LORD (Isaiah 37:14). When trouble lands on your desk, the first move is to bring it to Him.

Look at HOW he prays, too. He doesn't start with the problem. He starts with who God is: "You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth." (Isaiah 37:16) Then he says the hard facts out loud, that Assyria really has laid waste those countries (Isaiah 37:18). Praying doesn't mean pretending things aren't scary. It means telling the truth to the One who is bigger than the scary thing.

And check out his reason for asking. He wants to be saved "so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God." (Isaiah 37:20) He's not asking to protect his own spot, he's asking for God to be known. So, baker, the next time a big problem shows up, take it to the LORD first, tell Him the truth about it, and ask that He be honored in it. I'm telling you, this story is NOT over.
